title: Wipers and Washers: What Each Feature Does
introduction: I think of the wiper/washer switch as the rhythm control for a wet windshield: an occasional sweep, steady wiping or a response to changing rain. This overview identifies the available functions and distinguishes intermittent wiping from rain-sensitive operation. Exact switch movements, timing, speed relationships and lamp activation conditions belong to the operating instructions; this page is a feature guide.

edits.text: The wiper/washer switch activates the windshield wiper/washer system. Its functions range from clearing a little moisture to continuous wiping, with additional convenience and lighting features:
edits.why: Start with the switch as the driver's point of control, then use the feature names below to describe the behavior you are interested in.

edits.text: Mist wipe — on-demand wiping for light moisture.

edits.why: Washing and wiping are separate functions within the same system.

edits.text: Courtesy wipe — an additional convenience wiping function.
Windshield wipers — continuous wiping at low/high speed.
edits.why: These are the steady wiping modes, distinct from wiping with pauses.

edits.text: Intermittent wipers — wiping with pauses between cycles.
edits.why: Think of this as giving the windshield a breather between sweeps when continuous wiping would be more than the moisture calls for.

edits.text: Speed dependent wipers — wiping behavior linked to vehicle speed.
Wiper activated exterior lamps — exterior lighting activated through wiper operation.
edits.why: This feature links the windshield-clearing system with the car's exterior lighting.

edits.text: Rain sensitive wipers — wiping that responds to rain, if equipped.
edits.why: Check the fitted equipment before expecting this automatic response.

edits.text: There are 6 intermittent/sensitivity settings for the intermittent/rain sensitive wipers.
edits.why: I first identify which system is fitted: intermittent operation concerns the pauses between wipes, while rain-sensitive operation concerns the response to rain.
